name: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS)

degrees: B.E / B.Tech / M.E / M.Tech / MCA / M.Sc
eligibility.minMarks: 60% or 6.0 CGPA throughout 10th, 12th, Diploma, and Graduation
eligibility.backlogs: Maximum 1 active backlog permitted at test time; 0 backlogs at joining
eligibility.gap: Academic gap up to 24 months permitted with valid justification

sections.name: Numerical Ability (Quant)
sections.topics: Time & Work, Speed Distance & Time, Percentages, Profit & Loss, Ratio, Permutation & Probability, Number Systems

sections.name: Verbal Ability (English)
sections.topics: Reading Comprehension, Sentence Completion, Error Spotting, Para Jumbles

sections.name: Reasoning Ability (Logical)
sections.topics: Data Sufficiency, Syllogisms, Blood Relations, Coding-Decoding, Seating Arrangement

sections.name: Advanced Quant & Reasoning (Digital/Prime Qualifier)
sections.topics: Higher-level Math, Probability Distributions, Complex Logic puzzles

sections.name: Hands-on Coding (2 Questions)
sections.topics: Q1 (Easy-Medium): Array/String manipulation. Q2 (Medium-Hard): Dynamic Programming / Matrix / Graph / Math logic. Languages: C, C++, Java, Python

rounds.description: Foundation Section (Aptitude, Verbal, Logical) + Advanced Section (Advanced Quant & Coding). Score determines if you are interviewed for Ninja, Digital, or Prime.
Questions on resume projects, Core CS subjects (OOPs, DBMS, SQL queries, OS), and basic Data Structures (Arrays, Linked Lists, Sorting algorithms).
Behavioral scenarios, willingness to relocate, rotational shift agreement, background checks, and company culture fit.

syllabus: Aptitude: Work & Wages, Pipes & Cisterns, Mixtures & Alligations, Simple & Compound Interest
Logical: Clocks & Calendars, Statement-Conclusion, Non-Verbal reasoning
Technical: OOPs concepts, Normalization, SQL Joins, Pointers/References, Memory Allocation, Basics of Cloud & SDLC
tips: Time management on the iON platform is crucial: sections are strictly timed and navigation between sections is restricted.
In the coding round, focus on edge cases (negative numbers, empty inputs, large integer limits).
For Digital/Prime cadre, you must solve BOTH coding questions and score >75% in the Advanced Section.

name: Amazon

degrees: B.Tech / B.E / M.Tech in CS, IT, ECE or related engineering fields
eligibility.minMarks: 6.5+ CGPA or 65% aggregate with no standing backlogs
eligibility.gap: Standard career/education gaps evaluated on merit

sections.name: Online Assessment (OA1 / OA2): Coding
sections.topics: 1 Medium problem (Arrays, Sliding Window, Strings) + 1 Hard problem (Trees, Graphs, Priority Queues, Dynamic Programming)

sections.name: Work Style Assessment & Leadership Principles (LP)
sections.topics: Workplace scenarios testing Amazon's 16 Leadership Principles (Customer Obsession, Ownership, Bias for Action, Deliver Results)

sections.name: Code Explanation / Complexity Survey
sections.topics: Explaining the Time & Space complexity of your submitted solutions and alternate approaches

rounds.description: 2 algorithmic coding problems + Work Simulation & Amazon Leadership Principles assessment.
15 mins of Amazon Leadership Principles (STAR format) + 40 mins live coding (Trees, Graphs, or DP) + 5 mins Q&A.

rounds.type: Live Coding & Low Level Design (60 mins)
rounds.description: DSA problem solving + Object Oriented Design (e.g. Design a Parking Lot, Movie Booking, or File System) + LP questions.
Conducted by a certified independent Bar Raiser. Deep dive into past failures, conflicts, high-ambiguity situations, and system architecture.

syllabus: DSA: Binary Trees, BST, Graphs (BFS, DFS, Dijkstra), Heaps, Sliding Window, Monotonic Stack, Dynamic Programming (Knapsack, Grid DP)
CS Fundamentals: Operating Systems (Threads, Deadlocks), DBMS (Transactions, Indexing), OOPs Principles, Basic System Design
Leadership Principles: Customer Obsession, Ownership, Invent & Simplify, Are Right A Lot, Earn Trust, Deliver Results
tips: Leadership Principles carry equal 50% weightage with coding. Prepare 2 STAR stories for every LP.
Always communicate your thought process aloud before writing code. State brute force, then optimize.
Calculate and explain exact Time (Big-O) and Space complexity proactively.

name: Google

degrees: B.Tech / B.E / M.Tech / MS / PhD in Computer Science or related STEM disciplines
branches: Open to all branches with demonstrated software competence
eligibility.minMarks: No strict cut-off; 7.5+ CGPA recommended for on-campus screening
eligibility.backlogs: No active backlogs at time of joining

sections.name: Google Online Challenge (GOC)
sections.topics: Algorithmic challenges (Graph Theory, Combinatorics, Dynamic Programming, Segment Trees, Trie, Greedy)

rounds.description: Challenging algorithmic questions with strict execution time limits (1-2 seconds) and large test sets.
Pure algorithmic problem solving. You write code in Google Docs without auto-complete or syntax highlighting.
Focus on data structure optimization, recursion, graphs, or dynamic programming with follow-up constraints.
Advanced problem solving, memory limits handling, distributed computing considerations.
Evaluates intellectual humility, collaboration, navigation of ambiguity, ethical reasoning, and inclusive culture.

syllabus: Advanced DSA: Graph Algorithms (Topological sort, Tarjan's, Disjoint Set Union), DP on Trees, Segment Trees, Binary Search on Answer
Code Quality: Clean code, meaningful variable names, boundary checking, unit test cases
tips: Practice coding on a blank Google Doc without IDE assistance.
Check boundary constraints immediately (e.g. integer overflow, empty tree, disconnected graph).
Google interviewers evaluate how you respond to hints. Take feedback actively and adapt your solution.

degrees: B.E / B.Tech / M.E / M.Tech / MCA / M.Sc

eligibility.minMarks: 60% or 6.0 CGPA in 10th, 12th, and throughout Graduation

rounds.description: System Engineer: Aptitude & Pseudocode. SP/DSE: Algorithmic coding contest.
Covers projects on resume, basic SQL queries (joins, group by), OOPs in Java/Python, and simple coding (reverse string, prime check, palindrome).
Verification of academic documents, communication assessment, adaptability to training at Mysuru campus.

syllabus: Aptitude: Data sufficiency, Cryptarithmetic, Percentages, Ratio, Work & Time
Core CS: Object Oriented Programming, DBMS basics, Data Structures (Arrays, Linked Lists, Stacks, Queues)
tips: InfyTQ Certification allows direct entry to DSE/SP interviews if you score >65%.
In HackWithInfy, solving even 1 full question and 1 partial question often gets you a DSE interview call.

name: Microsoft

degrees: B.Tech / B.E / M.Tech / Dual Degree in CS, IT, ECE, EE
branches: Open across branches; strong coding portfolio required

sections.name: Coding Assessment
sections.topics: Medium to Hard coding questions on Arrays, Binary Search, Trees, Graphs, and Hash Tables. Evaluated on correctness, time complexity, and memory efficiency.

rounds.description: Tests both optimal algorithm design and corner case handling.
Problem solving with focus on Data Structures (Trees, Linked Lists, Stack) and modular coding.
Advanced DSA (Graphs/DP) or OOP System Design (Design an elevator controller, file search engine).
Evaluates cultural alignment, growth mindset, technical curiosity, and past project impact.

syllabus: DSA: Trees (LCA, Path Sum, Traversals), Linked Lists, Graphs (Shortest Path, Cycle Detection), Two Pointers, Trie
System Fundamentals: Concurrency, Thread safety, Memory management, Operating Systems, Web architecture
tips: Microsoft places great emphasis on the 'Growth Mindset' and learning from mistakes.
Write modular, readable code with descriptive variable names and comments.
Always dry run test cases with sample and extreme edge inputs.

name: Accenture

degrees: B.E / B.Tech / M.E / M.Tech / MCA / M.Sc
eligibility.minMarks: 65% or 6.5 CGPA with no standing backlogs
eligibility.gap: Up to 1 year gap allowed between education levels

sections.name: Cognitive Assessment (Analytical & Quant)
sections.topics: Critical Thinking, Problem Solving, English Ability, Abstract Reasoning

sections.name: Technical Assessment (Pseudocode & Fundamentals)
sections.topics: Pseudocode (bitwise operations, loops, recursion), Networking & Security, Cloud Fundamentals, MS Office

sections.name: Coding Assessment (Mandatory)
sections.topics: 1 Easy problem (String/Array logic) + 1 Medium problem (Mathematical / Array transformations). Language choices: C, C++, Java, Python

sections.name: Communication Assessment (Voice Test)
sections.topics: Reading sentences, Repeating sentences, Story retelling, Short question answers (Automated AI scoring)

rounds.description: Stage 1: Cognitive + Technical test. Immediate elimination round. If cleared, you immediately unlock the Coding test.
2 programming questions. Solving both unlocks the Advanced ASE (₹6.5 LPA) interview pipeline.
Non-elimination round assessing fluency, pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary.
Questions on final year project, basic concepts (OOPs, SQL), team player scenarios, and willingness to work across locations.

syllabus: Pseudocode: Bitwise operators (AND, OR, XOR), loop iterations, array index manipulation
Cloud & Networks: SaaS/PaaS/IaaS differences, OSI layers, IP addressing, basic firewalls
Aptitude: Syllogism, Blood relations, Sitting arrangement, Profit & loss, Percentages
tips: Practice pseudocode questions thoroughly; this section is where most candidates fail to clear the cutoff.
Ensure a clear headset and quiet environment for the Automated Communication round.
Be prepared to explain your major project role and the exact tech stack used.

rounds.round: Round 1: Wipro Elite National Talent Hunt (NTH)
rounds.description: Adaptive aptitude test (Quant, Logical, Verbal) + Essay Writing + 2 Coding problems. High performance on both coding questions qualifies for Turbo (₹6.5 LPA) interview.
In-depth review of academic projects, Core CS (OOPs, DBMS, basic SQL queries), programming language fundamentals, and basic data structures (Arrays, Strings, Linked Lists).
Communication assessment, willingness to relocate to any Wipro campus, night shifts agreement, and career aspirations.

syllabus: Quant: Averages, Simple/Compound Interest, Time & Work, Speed Distance Time, Profit & Loss, Permutations
Logical: Syllogism, Blood Relations, Statement & Assumptions, Seating Arrangements, Coding Decoding
Verbal: Grammar rules, Prepositions, Conjunctions, Idioms, Reading passages
Coding: Arrays, Two Pointers, String manipulation, Recursion, Basic Sorting and Searching
tips: In the Essay writing test, maintain strict grammar, correct punctuation, and use standard paragraphs; automated NLP evaluators penalize spelling and spacing mistakes heavily.
Solving 1 coding problem guarantees an Elite interview call; solving both coding problems with optimal time complexity makes you eligible for the Turbo cadre (₹6.5 LPA).
Review your resume projects thoroughly, including your exact personal contributions and database schemas.
